In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy-efficiency of a routing protocol depends on the network's application and requirements.

, the energy efficient routing protocols can be divided in two categories: the first one is the energy efficient routing protocol that is based on a specific communication scheme (Network Structure, Communication Model or Topology Based), and the second category is the energy efficient protocol that is based only on the reliable routing.

the most energy efficient routing protocols, which are proposed for WSN, are the protocols that are based on hierarchical structure, the negotiation-based communication model and the multipath routing scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most energy efficient protocols are those which use hierarchical routing and the ones that use negotiation based routing.

the proposed classification is very useful in order to have a better understanding of the proposed routing protocols and to have a better comparison between them, since the classification is based on their operation and not on their name.
the energy efficient routing protocols can be classified into four main categories, each one with its own characteristics and advantages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy consumption of WSNs depends on many factors, such as the network structure, communication model, topology and reliability of the routing protocols.
there is no single routing protocol that outperforms the others in all the aspects.
the classification of the routing protocols is not straightforward.
